script: US Radium Corporation knew it was poisoning its own workers, and lied anyway. In the 1910s, the company hired young women to paint watch dials with radium paint, and told them to point their brushes with their lips for a finer tip. Executives already had reports describing radium's injurious effects, and kept hiring painters anyway. When workers began dying of horrifying bone and jaw decay, the company altered a safety report to hide the truth from regulators. When painters' own doctors tried to warn the public, company lawyers threatened them into silence. When five dying survivors finally sued in 1927, the company's defense was to claim the women had syphilis instead. The lawsuit exposed the cover-up, and forced the workplace safety reforms the company fought to prevent. US Radium Corporation knew it was poisoning its workers, and lied until the truth outlived them.
